A quick introduction

I’m early in the journey — and intentional about it.

I’m a first-year student in the Faculty of Engineering and Technology (FET), CSE department, at South Asian University. I’m learning programming by practising the basics, experimenting with the browser and slowly taking on projects that require me to connect multiple concepts.

Right now, my core toolkit includes C, HTML, CSS and JavaScript. I’m also learning Python. Outside languages, I’m interested in optimisation, linear programming and the way a well-designed system can make a messy real-world process simpler.

I use VS Code, Git and GitHub, and work across Windows and Ubuntu Linux. I’m not trying to present myself as an expert — I’m here to build a strong foundation and keep improving.

Tools, languages & concepts

Learning in public

Interactive playground

See the logic.
Then write the code.

Two small browser-side experiments built to make concepts from my C and programming practice more visual.

Lab 01 / Bitwise

8-bit operator explorer

Change the inputs and inspect how AND, OR, XOR and NOT transform an 8-bit value.

8
// A and B shown as 8-bit binary
00001100 & 00001010 → 00001000

For NOT, this demo shows the low 8 bits only. C integer promotions and signedness can affect results in actual programs.

Lab 02 / Algorithms

Sorting visualizer

Watch adjacent comparisons and swaps. Switch between bubble sort and selection sort.

Comparing Sorted
A note about the demo

The visualizer runs in JavaScript inside this website to demonstrate algorithmic ideas that are also relevant when learning C. It is an educational companion, not an online C compiler.
